what_it_does: This paper describes a high-speed analog-to-digital converter (ADC)—a circuit that translates continuous analog signals into discrete digital numbers. The design challenge is building one that's compact and can scale to smaller chip sizes, but ring-oscillator-based designs (circuits that generate high-frequency signals) struggle to distinguish between different input values and are hard to tune without extensive calibration. This paper introduces a gated cyclic coupled ring-oscillator approach that shares the same measurement circuit across multiple parallel channels (processing 2 channels simultaneously at 2.2 billion samples per second each). The key insight is using a shared oscillator with built-in phase interpolation—a way to get finer measurement resolution—while reorganizing where the reference voltage is generated to reduce signal noise and maintain stable electrical impedance.
